newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean export registrations up 83 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean export registrations up 83 pct.

text.p: Export registrations for Brazilian soybeans in the 1997/98 marketing year (February/January) are currently 83 percent up on the same stage last year, said independent consultants Safras e Mercado.
According to the Overseas Trade Department, some 1.41 million tonnes of soybeans had been registered for export by October 31, up from 766,500 tonnes by the same stage last year.

However given expectations of total exports, registrations to-date account for roughly the same percentage, totalling 26 percent of the 5.4 million tonnes forecast for export against 21 percent of the 3.6 million estimated to be sold in 1996/97.

Registrations for soymeal exports which Safras expects to be slightly lower at 10.3 million tonnes against this year's 10.5 million tonnes are running 10 percent higher at 1.08 million against 983,600 tonnes to October 31, 1995.

Soyoil export registrations are however one percent down from this stage last year at 164,200 tonnes against 165,200 in 1996/97. Total soyoil exports are forecast at 1.35 million tonnes, up slightly from 1.3 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Total revenue from overseas sales of soybeans and soyproducts should reach $4.03 billion in 1997, practically the same as the $4.02 billion expected to be raised this year, Safras predicted.
The coming year's revenues are linked to the anticipated rise in soybean sales following the extinction of the ICMS state export tax in mid-September this year.

Before soybeans were subject to a 13 percent tax, soymeal 11.1 percent and soyoil a eight percent tax. This gave crushers a gross margin of around six percent for soymeal and soyoil exports but this has now been reduced to one percent with the scrapping of the tax which will naturally stimulate sales of soybeans, Safras said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
